answer: Bind each agent key to ferrous reality: a hardware TPM whose endorsement certificate is signed by the chip maker. At registration the agent proves its key lives in that chip, and the network stores only a hash of the endorsement key. A second agent key presenting the same hash in an epoch is refused, and virtual TPMs fail because no manufacturer signed them. A farm can't mirror one chip into a hundred VMs; it must buy a hundred chips, so each fake drags a cost like a comet's tail. (Tradeoff: trusts chip makers.)
